title: Molecular Dynamics Study on Wear Resistance of High Entropy Alloy Coatings Considering the Effect of Temperature

recollection.starting_material: Guess: an equimolar CoCrFeNiMn high‐entropy alloy coating deposited on a steel substrate
recollection.intervention: Guess: classical molecular‐dynamics simulations of a nanoscale sliding contact (e.g. a SiC or diamond tip) across the HEA surface at multiple temperatures (300 K, 600 K, 900 K)
recollection.structure: Guess: a single‐phase face‐centered cubic (FCC) solid solution with nanocrystalline grains (~5–10 nm) and a clean metal–substrate interface
recollection.mechanism: Guess: at low temperature, wear is dominated by dislocation nucleation and slip; at elevated temperature, enhanced atomic diffusion and tribo‐oxidation form an abrasive oxide layer that accelerates material removal
recollection.results: Guess: friction coefficient rises from ~0.20 at 300 K to ~0.35 at 900 K; wear rate increases from ~1×10⁻³ mm³/(N·m) to ~3×10⁻³ mm³/(N·m); estimated diffusion activation energy ~0.5 eV

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies temperature-dependent molecular-dynamics contact simulations and mentions several actual temperatures, but misses the nanoindentation protocol, loading depth/speed, unloading, and 1200 K condition. FCC structure is correct, while the alloy composition, nanocrystalline grains, and steel substrate are wrong. Low-temperature dislocation-mediated deformation is directionally relevant, but the proposed diffusion/tribo-oxidation mechanism is unsupported; the actual high-temperature mechanism is lattice disorder/softening with reduced dislocation density. All reported numerical friction, wear-rate, and activation-energy values are unsupported and omit the actual hardness and modulus changes.
